body:
Aeoleus wrote:
> 
> Woodswalker wrote:
> >
> > Here's a few quotes from some sick subversives who advocate overthrowing
> > the gov't.
> >
> >   "Mankind are disposed to suffer, while evils are sufferable, rthan to
> > right themselves by abolishing the forms to which they are accustomed.
> > But when a long train of abuses and usurpations, pursuing invariable the
> > same object, evinces a design to reduce them under absolute despotism, it
> > is their right, it is their duty, to throw off such government..."
> >   --THE DECLARATION OF INDEPENDENCE
> >
> >   "We therefore advocate a revolution against the industrial system." --
> >  THE UNABOMBER MANIFESTO
> 
> I don't think IS&F was about overthrowing the government at all..  While
> the Declaration of Independance and the Manifesto both have similar
> complaints, the Declaration is about the independance of a nation, whereas
> the Manifesto is about the independance of a person (or everyone,
> individually).  The Declaration advocated the establishment of a government,
> whereas the Manifesto advocated the dissolution of a government.  Ted,
> or the impression I got from his writing, was never one to believe in
> war or "revolution", as we think of revolution.  He believed in peace,
> and through peace, the development of a world without political borders,
> where people could cast off their industrial ties..  Now I won't trouble
> you with my own beliefs and my own philosophies, (of which some, if you
> are curious, can be found on my web page), but I just wanted to show you
> that your comparison between the two documents is mostly invalid.
> _____________________________________________________
> Brian Ream, Kalamazoo Michigan
> mailto:osiris@net-link.net http://www.net-link.net/~osiris

Thanks for something I wasn't expecting: an intelligent comment! You are 
right in everything you say; the UNA is for "small autonomous groups" 
rather than governments. He has probably read the SF book "Ecotopia" 
where California secedes and becomes a collection of pacifistic 
anarchist/ecological communes. But the reason why I drew the comparison 
was to show that both parties were fighting for "freedom", and both were 
willing to break the law for that aim. Which is how UNA is different from 
a criminal who just kills for kicks or personal gain. --Laura
